transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The latest poll out from NPR PBS News Marist finds that many American voters are taking
President Trump's work into consideration as they think about whom to vote for.
NPR's Stephen Fowler has more.
Overall, 45 percent of voters say their choice is against Trump.
That's most Democrats and just over half of independents.
But you've got a large number of Republicans, including two in five who voted for him in
2024, who say that Trump is not much of a factor in their vote.
You can read that two ways.
One, more people are supporting Democrats, including some people that voted for Trump
before.
And two, there's a potential for Trump's base to stay home this year and/or Republicans
to break from Trump and back a Democrat in some of these key races.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reporting.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will address the United Nations General Assembly
later today.
He is expected to focus on Russia's full-scale invasion of his country.
And Piers Michelle Kellerman reports Zelensky has already held talks with President Trump
at the U.N., hoping to find ways to end the war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says President Trump wants to end the war and has
questioned Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy facilities.
Zelensky says he told Trump that Ukraine would stop such attacks when Russia ends its bombardment
of civilian infrastructure in Ukraine.
"We are ready for energy ceasefire, it doesn't matter if they will not, if they don't want
us to attack their diesel and their fineries and etc.
So we are ready if they will not attack our energy system, our electricity hitting system."
But he's preparing for another tough winter.
Zelensky is asking Trump to raise this with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later this week
since China has influence with Russia.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, The United Nations.
OpenAI is calling for the U.S. to lead in setting global AI safety standards.
NPR's John Ruich reports several AI industry leaders will brief the U.N. Security Council
today.
"OpenAI is releasing its proposal at a time of intense debate about how to regulate artificial
intelligence after a string of incidents that have raised concern about the technology."
It says international safety and security standards are key to answering the question,
what does good look like in the mitigation of catastrophic AI risk?
AI companies and labs have to take accountability for developing AI safely, it says, but standards
will help more stakeholders have a say in how AI evolves.
OpenAI says the United States should lead an effort with other countries to develop technical
standards for the most cutting-edge artificial intelligence, including for recursive self-improvement,
or AI-building AI, which many believe could lead to the technology spiraling out of human
control.
John Ruich, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
Forecasters say that Hurricane Polo's top sustained winds have dropped to 155 miles per
hour as it swirls off Mexico's western coast.
The Category 4 storm is expected to stay offshore.
Forecasters say Polo is one of the most powerful ever seen in that region.
It was a small tropical system on Monday.
It reached the top Category 5 hurricane status in less than a day.
Higher child care costs are pushing more families to seek help from a familiar source, grandparents.
NPR's Joe Hernandez reports older generations are increasingly stepping in to fill the child
care gap.
Grandparents helping with child care is not new, but the rising cost of daycare and other
options has made family support critical.
A recent study from AARP found grandparents who provide some care but aren't full-time
caregivers watch their grandchildren a median amount of 3.8 hours per week.
Nicole Jorwick, with the national organization Caring Across Generations, says many parents
want their parents to be able to enjoy retirement and later phases of life.
But because of the lack of child care in this country, adult children are relying on their
parents for that labor.
And it is labor.
According to Child Care Aware of America, the average cost of child care in the U.S. for
last year was more than $13,000.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
Delivery company DoorDash says it'll pay more than $131 million to settle claims.
DoorDash says it underpaid New York City delivery workers.
This is NPR.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to address UN General Assembly today on Russia's invasion
Zelensky tells Trump Ukraine ready for energy ceasefire if Russia stops attacking infrastructure
OpenAI calls for U.S. to lead in setting global AI safety standards at UN
Hurricane Polo drops to Category 4 with 155 mph winds off Mexico's western coast
Rising child care costs push more families to rely on grandparents for assistance
DoorDash to pay $131 million to settle underpayment claims for New York City workers
